Its primary function is to keep track of the current top of the stack, which is the address of the most recently allocated memory location. When a program allocates memory on the stack, the operating system stores the address of that location in the esp register. This allows the program to access the allocated memory and perform operations on it. The esp register is also used to store the return address of a function, which is the address of the instruction that will be executed when the function returns. This allows the function to access its local memory space and perform operations on it.
